To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ortho fluorine effects are very large for C-H bond activation by [Tp'R(CNneop)H], but are not as large as predicted by theoretical studies.

1) ortho fluorine effects are important in determining the stability and reactivity of Rh-C(aryl(F))H complexes, 2) ortho fluorines stabilize the Rh-C(alkyl) bond, 3) ortho fluorinations of aryl groups can be used to tune the reactivity of Rh(III) complexes and, 4) the ortho fluorine stabilization of the Rh-C bond is related to the strength of the C-H bond.
ortho fluorination of aromatic hydrocarbons increases the strength of the C-H bond, decreases the stability of the resulting Rh-C(aryl)(H) bond and increases the stability of the C-F bond.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the activation of C-H bonds in aromatic compounds and the subsequent formation of C-C bonds.
the reactivity of a series of aromatic fluorides with a rhodium(I) complex containing a neopentyl ligand, and the effect of ortho fluorine substitution on the C-H bond activation process.
the activation of C-H bonds in fluorinated aromatic hydrocarbon substrates by a series of [Tp'Rh] complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ortho fluorine effects are not only important in the activation of the C-H bond, but they are also important in determining the stability of the Rh(III)-aryl product.
the ortho fluorines stabilize the Rh-C bond by a combination of steric and electronic effects.
the ortho fluorine effects are real, and that they can be quantified by experiment, but that the exact mechanism of the effect is not yet understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ortho fluorine substituent has a large effect on the stability of the Rh-aryl intermediate, but a much smaller effect on the strength (or weakness) of the Rh-C bond.
the presence of ortho fluorine substituens increases the stability of the Rh(III) complex by destabilizing the C-H bond.
the ortho fluorine substituent stabilizes the C-H bond in the aromatic hydrocarbon by 2.2 kcal mol(-1), but destabilizes the Rh-C(ary)l bond by 5 kcal mol-1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-H activation barrier is not directly proportional to the C-H bond strength, but rather the C-H bond energy is a poor indicator of the C-H activation energy.
fluorinated aromatic C-H bonds are much more difficult to break than their hydrogenated analogues.
ortho fluorination of aromatic rings can have a profound effect on the stability and reactivity of metal-aryl bonds.
